output.summary: A 49-year-old with long-standing endometriosis and early perimenopause asked whether endometriosis improves after menopause. The bot explained that while estrogen-driven endo typically quiets in menopause for most people, deeper disease with adhesions may persist, and that HRT—if needed for hot flashes and sleep—should be combined estrogen-plus-progestogen rather than unopposed estrogen to avoid reactivating residual lesions. The user accepted this nuanced answer as more useful than reassurance alone and felt prepared to discuss HRT carefully with their primary care doctor.
